 Medium
 Large
 Print The victims were all males in the age group 32-50 GUWAHATI: At least 12 people died between Wednesday and Friday and over 180 are in hospitals after mass consumption of suspected adulterated liquor in Manipur ’s Chakpikarong sub-division and adjoining areas in Chandel district. All the fatalities are males and their ages run from 32 to 50. Most of the deaths are from five villages in the sub-division. CM Y Khemchand Singh visited Shija Hospitals and Research Institute in Imphal West district and Babina Hospital in Imphal East district on Friday evening and enquired about the health of those admitted. He promised an enquiry and punishment for the culprits. In a social media post, the CM wrote that over 140 patients were admitted in Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The chief minister informed that to tackle the emerging situation, a medical team including specialists in general medicine along with medicines has been sent to Chandel district. The district deputy commissioner’s office stated that the exact cause of death is yet to be established medically and scientifically and is under investigation while issuing an advisory as a precaution, urging people to stay away from locally brewed liquor or alcohol of doubtful origin in the affected areas until further notice. The administration also said that anyone with vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision or breathing difficulty after drinking should seek immediate medical care and not wait for symptoms to worsen. The administration asked people who drank from the same suspected source to get checked even without symptoms. Chandel district superintendent of police Dharmendra Kumar in his report stated that the “alcohol which was reported consumed were bought from Sugnu, (in neighbouring) Kakching district.” He clarified that there is no known local brewing or manufacturing of traditional or local wine in Chandel district.
